BiblicalUsage: massôʼ is partiality, a lifting up of a face in favour, and it occurs once, in 2 Chronicles 19:7. There Jehoshaphat tells the judges that there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts. The word is the favour God refuses to show.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe massôʼ teaches me that God shows no partiality, and I hold that my own judgments should be as free of favour as His.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
